title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
summary: Find the median of two sorted arrays in logarithmic time without merging them.

tests.explain: Merged: [1, 2, 3]. The median is the middle value, 2.
Merged: [1, 2, 3, 4]. With an even count the median is the mean of the middle pair: (2 + 3) / 2 = 2.5.

hints: Merging both arrays and picking the middle is O(m + n). To do better, think about how many elements from each array end up in the left half of the merged order.

If you take i elements from the shorter array, you must take half - i from the other, where half = floor((m + n + 1) / 2). The split is right when every left element is <= every right element: A[i-1] <= B[j] and B[j-1] <= A[i]. Binary search i.

Search i in [0, m] on the shorter array. If A[i-1] > B[j], move i left; if B[j-1] > A[i], move i right. Treat out-of-range neighbours as minus or plus Infinity. The median is max(left side) when m + n is odd, otherwise (max(left) + min(right)) / 2.

complexity.time: O(log(min(m, n))): binary search on the shorter array
